title: close-security-issues workflow: filter issue titles in the job `if:` so unrelated issues never start a runner
answers: Why does the security-issue auto-close workflow start a runner for every opened issue?
How do I change which issue titles trigger the automatic security-vulnerability close comment?
Where is the title match for the security vulnerability auto-close handled?
Why did the close job's shell step stop checking the issue title with grep?
body:
Path: .github/workflows/close-security-issues.yml:close is the job that runs on newly opened issues and auto-closes ones that look like security vulnerability reports, posting the private-reporting guidance comment via `gh issue close`. Title and repository gating for this job lives here.
Rule: Put event filters (repository, issue title terms) in the job-level `if:` expression, not in a shell step. GitHub evaluates job `if:` before provisioning a runner, so non-matching issues skip the runner entirely. Title terms are checked with `contains(github.event.issue.title, ...)`, which is case-insensitive, so no `tr`/`grep` normalization is needed.
Symptom: Every newly opened issue in mlflow/mlflow spun up an ubuntu-slim runner just to run a title grep and exit, even when the issue was unrelated to security.
Constraints: Applies to this workflow's job-level gating. The current `if:` requires both the words 'security' and 'vulnerability' anywhere in the title, which is looser than the old `security\s+vulnerability` regex (words no longer need to be adjacent). Keep the close command and guidance comment unchanged when editing the step body.
applies: Event-based gating of the close-security-issues GitHub Actions workflow in mlflow/mlflow; not for other workflows.
says: The security issue auto-close workflow starts a runner for every new issue; how do I stop that?
Unrelated issues trigger the security vulnerability close job; can the title filter run earlier?
Security auto-close comment fires on issues that only mention security; how is the title matched?
search: close-security-issues workflow: title and repository filters belong in the job-level if expression so non-matching issues never start a runner. Title terms use case-insensitive contains on the issue title. The current check requires both security and vulnerability anywhere in the title, not adjacent. Close command and guidance comment stay unchanged.
